newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Industry welcomes Commission nuclear programme.
newsitem.headline: Industry welcomes Commission nuclear programme.

text.p: The European nuclear industry and Eurelectric, the European grouping of the electricity supply industry, welcomed on Monday the Commission's draft "Indicative Nuclear Programme", which was made public last September.

However, FORATOM, the association of the European nuclear industry, urged the Commission to strengthen its support for nuclear energy, saying the industry represented a major investment in advanced technology and jobs.
"The industry deserves support. Current nuclear plants are generating competitively priced electricity," it said in a statement.
In addition, it said EU nuclear plants prevented around 700 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.
The Commission's programme recognised the "important role which nuclear energy is playing in the supply of energy as well as in industrial and technological development," it said.
Eurelectric said the programme provided a useful and timely basis for discussion of the future of the nuclear industry in the EU.

But concerning security of supply it failed to face up fully to the issues it raised, in particular the potential for nuclear power to counterbalance the expected growth in the EU's dependence on imported energy.

"If the nuclear power plants which will begin to be decommissioned after 2010 are not replaced with new nuclear plants the EU's dependence on imported energy will increase still further," a Eurelectric statement said.
In its draft programme, the Commission proposed common principles for Europe's use of nuclear power, saying it was contributing to the EU's energy supply and economic welfare.
There are more than 140 nuclear reactors operating in eight of the EU's 15 member states, generating one third of the bloc's electricity and making it the world's leading producer.

The Commission said the use of nuclear energy had a favourable impact on the security of supply, qualified jobs, fuel imports and reductions of carbon dioxide emissions. Nuclear energy helped to reduce fossil fuel consumption and the subsequent reduced demand on the international oil market had made a contribution towards "moderating" oil prices.
On the other hand, the Commission said there were questions related to the concerns on safety, transport, management of waste, decommissioning and non-proliferation.
Further technological development and increased international cooperation was needed, it said.
Among the suggested principles, the Commission said each member state had the right to decide whether to develop the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
